newsitem.title: USA: "Air Force One" still flies high at box office.
newsitem.headline: "Air Force One" still flies high at box office.

text.p: Harrison Ford's "Air Force One" fended off competition from a handful of new releases to retain the top position at the North American box office for a second weekend, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
The presidential hijack thriller earned about $26.2 million for the Friday-to-Sunday period, which brings its 10-day total to $81.2 million.
"Spawn," a big-screen version of the comic book series about a black superhero, opened in second with $21.5 million, which includes Thursday-night sneak previews of about $1.5 million.

"George of the Jungle" slipped to third in its third weekend with $8.4 million, taking its total to $64.2 million. "Men in Black" was fourth with $8.0 million in its fifth weekend, as its total rose to $208.1 million.

"Picture Perfect," a romantic comedy starring "Friends" so- star Jennifer Aniston, opened in fifth with $7.5 million. Walt Disney Co.'s( ) canine sports comedy "Air Bud" opened in seventh with $4.7 million. This excludes figures for Canada, where Disney did not have the distribution rights.

A spokesman for Columbia Pictures, which released "Air Force One," said the film's weekend tally sets a new record for a three-day August gross. The old record was held by "The Fugitive," also starring Ford, which opened to $23.7 million during the Aug. 6-8 weekend of 1993. Columbia, which also released "Men in Black" is owned by Sony Corp. ( )
Among other notable performances, ninth-placed "Face/Off" passed the $100 million mark on Saturday as its total after six weekends rose to $102.1 million.

"Spawn" is released by New Line Cinema, a unit of Time Warner Inc. "George of the Jungle" is released by Disney. "Picture Perfect" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp.. "Face/Off" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..
